answer: A bank of pre-written answers therefore has nothing to key against, and filling 202 aliases means authoring 202 texts that each match their own nonce. Because the derivation is bound to the knoll signature, the bridge gate rejects a mismatch, and the kernel checkpoint keeps the derivation inputs for replay. Each challenge carries a 69 bit nonce derived from the identity key and the epoch seed, so no two identities ever answer the same question. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
